finding.claim: wipe() never enforces the OWNER role: requireRole() returns a boolean that is discarded, so any caller (including users with no roles) can wipe any tenant.
finding.source: Caller-supplied User u (roles) and attacker-chosen tenant path parameter {t} on POST /tenants/{t}/wipe (comment at Admin.java:24).
finding.sink: repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27, a destructive tenant-wide delete.

trace.note: wipe(User u, String tenant) accepts caller roles and attacker-chosen tenant.
Calls requireRole(u, "OWNER") and ignores the boolean result.
requireRole returns u.roles().contains(role) and never throws (documented at line 13).

finding.guards_checked: requireRole (lines 14-16): returns boolean, result ignored by caller, no enforcement. checkRole (lines 18-22): throws correctly but is not used by wipe(). No tenant-ownership check. No null checks on u, tenant, or repo.

verdict.guard_found: requireRole (src/Admin.java:14-16) returns a boolean and is called as a bare statement at src/Admin.java:26, so its result is discarded and nothing aborts. checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) would throw, but wipe() does not call it; export() at line 32 does. No tenant-ownership check exists. The repo contains only src/Admin.java, so no route-level middleware is visible.
verdict.reason: wipe() at src/Admin.java:26 calls requireRole, which returns a boolean (line 15), and the result is discarded, so repo.wipe(tenant) at line 27 runs for any User regardless of roles. The attacker only needs to reach the caller of wipe(); the HTTP layer that exposes POST /tenants/{t}/wipe is not in the repo, so reachability by an authenticated low-privilege user is inferred from the comment at line 24, not verified.

finding.claim: OWNER is checked against a global per-user role set with no tenant binding, so a user who is OWNER of one tenant can export (and, via wipe(), delete) a different tenant. Plausible: depends on whether roles are meant to be tenant-scoped and whether the caller pre-scopes the User.
finding.source: Authenticated user holding OWNER for their own tenant, supplying a different {t} in POST /tenants/{t}/export.
finding.sink: repo.export(tenant) at src/Admin.java:33 (cross-tenant data export); repo.wipe(tenant) at src/Admin.java:27 for the same class of issue.

trace.note: record User(String name, Set<String> roles) carries no tenant; roles are global to the user.
export(User u, String tenant) takes attacker-chosen tenant.
checkRole(u, "OWNER") tests the global role set only; tenant is never compared.
repo.export(tenant) runs for any tenant the caller names.

finding.guards_checked: checkRole (lines 18-22) correctly throws when OWNER is absent, so F1 does not apply to export. No tenant-to-user membership check exists in this file. The caller that builds User is outside this repo, so any pre-scoping cannot be verified.

verdict.guard_found: checkRole (src/Admin.java:18-22) is the only control on export. It tests the global role set and throws on failure, so it is effective against non-OWNER callers but never compares the tenant. No tenant-to-user membership check exists in this repo.
verdict.reason: The trace matches the code: User has no tenant field (src/Admin.java:4), export accepts any tenant (src/Admin.java:31), and checkRole only tests the global role set (src/Admin.java:32). Whether a user's OWNER role is tenant-scoped depends on how the caller builds the User, which is outside this repo, so cross-tenant exploitation can be neither confirmed nor refuted here.
